title: Search of Vanaras in Riksha cavity,
introduction: Monkeys enter Riksha cavity, an unsightly and gloomy one, during their search in southern direction. While groping in that dark they loose time set by Sugreeva. Finally, they see luminosity and extraordinarily built mansions, woodlands, trees and lakes. Thereupon they catch sight of an elderly sainted lady and they all approach her asking after the legend of that cavity.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे पंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 50th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
सह तारा अंगदाभ्याम् तु संगम्य हनुमान् कपिः |
विचिनोति च विन्ध्यस्य गुहाः च गहनानि च
verses.iast:
saha tārā aṃgadābhyām tu saṃgamya hanumān kapiḥ |
vicinoti ca vindhyasya guhāḥ ca gahanāni ca
verses.translation: Associated with Angada, Lt. Tara and others, the monkey Hanuma searched the caves and thick forests of Vindhya Range.

glosses.meaning: Lt. Tara, Angada and others, along with
Vindhya's, caves, also, thick forests, also

verses.devanagari:
सिंह शार्दूल जुष्टाः च गुहाः च परितः तथा |
विषमेषु नग इन्द्रस्य महा प्रस्रवणेषु च
verses.iast:
siṃha śārdūla juṣṭāḥ ca guhāḥ ca paritaḥ tathā |
viṣameṣu naga indrasya mahā prasravaṇeṣu ca
verses.translation: Hanuma has searched in the caves of that kingly Mt. Vindhya, which are jammed in with lions and tigers, and even at the towering rapids.

glosses.meaning: by lions, tigers, jammed in, also

verses.devanagari:
आसेदुः तस्य शैलस्य कोटिम् दक्षिण पस्चिमाम् |
तेषाम् तत्र एव वसताम् स कालो व्यत्यवर्तत
verses.iast:
āseduḥ tasya śailasya koṭim dakśiṇa pascimām |
teṣām tatra eva vasatām sa kālo vyatyavartata
verses.translation: They reached the southwest peak of that mountain during their search and the time set by Sugreeva swiftly lapsed while they are overstaying thereat that Mt. Vindhya alone.

glosses.meaning: for them, thereat, alone, on staying [overstaying]

verses.devanagari:
स हि देशो दुरन्वेष्यो गुहा गहनवान् महान् |
तत्र वायु सुतः सर्वम् विचिनोति स्म पर्वतम्
verses.iast:
sa hi deśo duranveṣyo guhā gahanavān mahān |
tatra vāyu sutaḥ sarvam vicinoti sma parvatam
verses.translation: Though that extensive province is indeed an unsearchable one with its impenetrable caves and forests, yet Hanuma, the son of Air-god, searched everywhere on that mountain.

verses.devanagari:
परस्परेण रहिता अन्योन्यस्य अविदूरतः |
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः
मैन्दः च द्विविदः चैव हनुमान् जांबवान् अपि |
अंगदो युव राजः च तारः च वनगोचरः
गिरि जाल आवृतान् देशान् मार्गित्वा दक्षिणाम् दिशम् |
विचिन्वन्तः ततः तत्र ददृशुः विवृतम् बिलम्
दुर्गम् ऋक्ष बिलम् नाम दानवेन अभिरक्षितम् |
verses.iast:
paraspareṇa rahitā anyonyasya avidūrataḥ |
gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ
maindaḥ ca dvividaḥ caiva hanumān jāmbavān api |
aṃgado yuva rājaḥ ca tāraḥ ca vanagocaraḥ
giri jāla āvṛtān deśān mārgitvā dakṣiṇām diśam |
vicinvantaḥ tataḥ tatra dadṛśuḥ vivṛtam bilam
durgam ṛkśa bilam nāma dānavena abhirakśitam |
verses.translation: Without pressing one another closely, yet not distancing from one another largely, Gaja, Gavaaksha, Gavaya, Sharabha, Gandhamaadana, also thus Mainda, Dvivida, and Hanuma, and even Jaambavanta, crown prince Angada, also the forest-mover Lt. Tara have searched that province in southern direction that is encompassed with interlocked mountains, and during their search there they have observed a wide-opened and impassable cavity known as Riksha cavity which is well guarded by a demon called Maya.

glosses.meaning: mutually, without - distancing from one another
mountains, mesh of, encompassed by, province

verses.devanagari:
क्षुत् पिपासा परीताः तु श्रान्ताः तु सलिल अर्थिनः
अवकीर्णम् लता वृक्षैः ददृशुः ते महा बिलम् |
verses.iast:
kṣut pipāsā parītāḥ tu śrāntāḥ tu salila arthinaḥ
avakīrṇam latā vṛkṣaiḥ dadṛśuḥ te mahā bilam |
verses.translation: Thirst and hunger invading them they are fatigued and craving for water, and such as they are they beheld that capacious cavity which is enwrapped in climbers and trees.

glosses.meaning: hunger, thirst, wrapped up in [invaded by]

verses.devanagari:
तत्र क्रौन्चाः च हंसाः च सारसाः च अपि निष्क्रमन्
जल आर्द्राः चक्रवाकाः च रक्त अंगाः पद्म रेणुभिः |
verses.iast:
tatra krauncāḥ ca haṃsāḥ ca sārasāḥ ca api niṣkraman
jala ārdrāḥ cakravākāḥ ca rakta aṃgāḥ padma reṇubhiḥ |
verses.translation: There they have seen the swans and the waterfowls like Kraunca, Saarasa, and even Cakravaka waterfowls exiting from the cavity with their bodies drenched in water and reddened with the dapples of lotuses' pollen.

glosses.itrans: krauncaaH ca hamsaaH ca saarasaaH ca
glosses.iast: krauncāḥ ca hamsāḥ ca sārasāḥ ca
glosses.devanagari: क्रौन्चाः च हम्साः च सारसाः च
glosses.meaning: Kaunca waterfowls, also, swans, also, Saarasa waterfowls, also

verses.devanagari:
ततः तत् बिलम् आसाद्य सुगन्धि दुरतिक्रमम्
विस्मय व्यग्र मनसो बभूवुः वानरर्षभाः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ tat bilam āsādya sugandhi duratikramam
vismaya vyagra manaso babhūvuḥ vānararṣabhāḥ |
verses.translation: When those best vanara-s have neared that fragrant and impermeable cavity they are disheartened with amazement.

glosses.meaning: with amaze, dismayed, at heart [disheartened with amazement]

verses.devanagari:
संजात परिशंकाः ते तत् बिलम् प्लवग उत्तमाः
अभ्यपद्यन्त संहृष्टाः तेजोवन्तो महाबलाः |
verses.iast:
saṃjāta pariśaṃkāḥ te tat bilam plavaga uttamāḥ
abhyapadyanta saṃhṛṣṭāḥ tejovanto mahābalāḥ |
verses.translation: Though a suspicion in general is evoked in them, as they presumed that cavity to be Naraka, The Hell of Yama, or Paataala, the Netherworld of Emperor Bali, those highly resplendent and great mighty fly-jumpers have neared it, rejoicing for the availability of water in there.

glosses.meaning: evoked, general, suspicion - a high suspicion is evoked in them

verses.devanagari:
नाना सत्त्व समाकीर्णाम् दैत्य इन्द्र निलय उपमम्
दुर्दर्शम् इव घोरम् च दुर्विगाह्यम् च सर्वशः |
verses.iast:
nānā sattva samākīrṇām daitya indra nilaya upamam
durdarśam iva ghoram ca durvigāhyam ca sarvaśaḥ |
verses.translation: That hideous cavity is dispersed with diverse beings, similar to the residence of the emperor of demons, namely Emperor Bali, in Paataala, the Netherworld, and it is unsightly and impermeable from anywhere.

glosses.meaning: impossible, verily, to enter [un-enterable cavity,] also.

verses.devanagari:
ततः पर्वत कूट आभो हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
अब्रवीत् वानरान् घोरान् कान्तार वन कोविदः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ parvata kūṭa ābho hanumān māruta ātmajaḥ
abravīt vānarān ghorān kāntāra vana kovidaḥ |
verses.translation: The son of Air-god Hanuma whose glossiness is like that of a mountaintop and who is a mastermind in scrutinising every inscrutable forest, then spoke to all of the formidable Vanara-s.

glosses.meaning: to formidable ones [or, to all of the,] Vanara-s, spoke to.

verses.devanagari:
गिरि जाल आवृतान् देशान् मार्गित्वा दक्षिणाम् दिशम्
वयम् सर्वे परिश्रांता न च पश्याम मैथिलीम् |
verses.iast:
giri jāla āvṛtān deśān mārgitvā dakṣiṇām diśam
vayam sarve pariśrāṃtā na ca paśyāma maithilīm |
verses.translation: "We all have searched the southern quarter including those places that are enmeshed with meshes of mountains, and we are overly fatigued, but Maithili is unnoticed.

verses.devanagari:
अस्मात् च अपि बिलात् हंसाः क्रौन्चाः च सह सारसैः
जल आर्द्राः चक्रवाकाः च निष्पतन्ति स्म सर्वशः |
नूनम् सलिलवान् अत्र कूपो वा यदि वा ह्रदः
तथा च इमे बिल द्वारे स्निग्धाः तिष्ठन्ति पादपाः |
verses.iast:
asmāt ca api bilāt haṃsāḥ krauncāḥ ca saha sārasaiḥ
jala ārdrāḥ cakravākāḥ ca niṣpatanti sma sarvaśaḥ |
nūnam salilavān atra kūpo vā yadi vā hradaḥ
tathā ca ime bila dvāre snigdhāḥ tiṣṭhanti pādapāḥ |
verses.translation: "Swans along with waterfowls like Saarasa, Kruanca, and water drenched Cakravaka birds are coming out of this cavity from all over, and even the trees available at its doorway are verdant. Certainly there must be a wellspring, or otherwise a pond with water." Thus Hanuma spoke to all monkeys.

glosses.meaning: swans, along with, also, Saarasa waterfowls
from all over, out falling - coming out, they are
glisten, they are - they are verdant.

verses.devanagari:
इति उक्ताः तत् बिलम् सर्वे विविशुः तिमिर आवृतम्
अचन्द्र सूर्यम् हरयो ददृशू रोम हर्षणम् |
verses.iast:
iti uktāḥ tat bilam sarve viviśuḥ timira āvṛtam
acandra sūryam harayo dadṛśū roma harṣaṇam |
verses.translation: When Hanuma spoke to them thus as a kind of assurance, all those monkeys entered the cavity and found it as a sunless or moonless cavity, enfolded in hair-raising darkness.

verses.devanagari:
निशम्य तस्मात् सिंहाः च तान् तान् च मृग पक्षिणः
प्रविष्टा हरि शार्दूला बिलम् तिमिर आवृतम् |
verses.iast:
niśamya tasmāt siṃhāḥ ca tān tān ca mṛga pakśiṇaḥ
praviṣṭā hari śārdūlā bilam timira āvṛtam |
verses.translation: Those tigerly monkeys have also seen lions and various other animals and birds exiting therefrom, and entered that cavity which is enshrouded in obscurity.

verses.devanagari:
न तेषाम् सज्जते दृष्टिः न तेजः न पराक्रमः
वायोः इव गतिः तेषाम् दृष्टिः तम् अपि वर्तते |
verses.iast:
na teṣām sajjate dṛṣṭiḥ na tejaḥ na parākramaḥ
vāyoḥ iva gatiḥ teṣām dṛṣṭiḥ tam api var.htate |
verses.translation: Their eyesight, or their vigour, or their valorousness is rendered ineffectual, and their permeation is just like the directionless air as their eyesight is thwarted in gloominess.

glosses.meaning: eyesight, not, fit enough [became unfit, ineffectual / obstructed]

verses.devanagari:
ते प्रविष्टाः तु वेगेन तत् बिलम् कपि कुंजराः
प्रकाशम् च अभिरामम् च ददृशुः देशम् उत्तमम् |
verses.iast:
te praviṣṭāḥ tu vegena tat bilam kapi kuṃjarāḥ
prakāśam ca abhirāmam ca dadṛśuḥ deśam uttamam |
verses.translation: But on their going further into that cavity speedily, those elephantine monkeys beheld a best place that is luminous, as well as lovely.

glosses.meaning: that, cavity, speedily, on entering [going further,] but

verses.devanagari:
ततः तस्मिन् बिले भीमे नाना पादप संकुले
अन्योन्यम् संपरिष्वज्य जग्मुर् योजनम् अंतरम् |
verses.iast:
tataḥ tasmin bile bhīme nānā pādapa saṃkule
anyonyam sampariṣvajya jagmur yojanam aṃtaram |
verses.translation: In that awful cave that is compacted with various trees, then they advanced further an interstice of yojana distance, hand in hand lest one may miss the other.

glosses.meaning: each, to each, tightly, bracing [hand in hand]

verses.devanagari:
ते नष्ट संज्ञाः तृषिताः संभ्रांताः सलिल अर्थिनः
परिपेतुर् बिले तस्मिन् कंचित् कालम् अतन्द्रिताः |
verses.iast:
te naṣṭa saṃjñāḥ tṛṣitāḥ sambhrāṃtāḥ salila arthinaḥ
paripetur bile tasmin kaṃcit kālam atandritāḥ |
verses.translation: Though they are craving for water, highly perplexed, and lost track of their destination or any waterway, and yet hopeful of their mission they unwearyingly hopped in that cavity for a good while.

glosses.meaning: for some, time [for a good while]

verses.devanagari:
ते कृशा दीन वदनाः परिश्रान्ताः प्लवंगमाः
आलोकम् ददृशुः वीरा निराशा जीविते यदा |
verses.iast:
te kṛśā dīna vadanāḥ pariśrāntāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
ālokam dadṛśuḥ vīrā nirāśā jīvite yadā |
verses.translation: Those fly-jumpers are presently enervated and overly tired, and sad faced, and when those brave ones are despaired of their life, just then they perceived a luminescence.

verses.devanagari:
ततः तम् देशम् आगम्य सौम्याः वितिमिरम् वनम्
ददृशुः कान्चनान् वृक्षान् दीप्त वैश्वानर प्रभान् |
सालान् तालान् तमालान् च पुन्नागान् वंजुलान् धवान्
चंपकान् नाग वृक्षान् च कर्णिकारान् च पुष्पितान् |
स्तबकैः कांचनैः चित्रैः रक्तैः किसलयैः तथा
आपीडैः च लताभिः च हेम आभरण भूषितैः |
तरुण आदित्य संकाशान् वैदूर्यमय वेदिकान्
विभ्राजमानान् वपुषा पादपान् च हिरण्मयान् |
नील वैदूर्य वर्णाः च पद्मिनीः पतगैः आवृताः
महद्भिः कांचनैः वृक्षैः वृता बाल अर्क संनिभैः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ tam deśam āgamya saumyāḥ vitimiram vanam
dadṛśuḥ kāncanān vṛkṣān dīpta vaiśvānara prabhān |
sālān tālān tamālān ca punnāgān vaṃjulān dhavān
campakān nāga vṛkṣān ca karṇikārān ca puṣpitān |
stabakaiḥ kāṃcanaiḥ citraiḥ raktaiḥ kisalayaiḥ tathā
āpīḍaiḥ ca latābhiḥ ca hema ābharaṇa bhūṣitaiḥ |
taruṇa āditya saṃkāśān vaidūryamaya vedikān
vibhrājamānān vapuṣā pādapān ca hiraṇmayān |
nīla vaidūrya varṇāḥ ca padminīḥ patagaiḥ āvṛtāḥ
mahadbhiḥ kāṃcanaiḥ vṛkṣaiḥ vṛtā bāla arka saṃnibhaiḥ |
verses.translation: Those amenable monkeys on arriving at that province then beheld a shadowless woodland with golden trees which in irradiance is like the irradiated Ritual-fire. They beheld Saala, Taala [Palmyra,] Tamaala trees and some flowered trees like Punnaaga, Vanjula, Dhava, Campaka, Naaga, also Karnikaara trees. The bunches of their flowers are golden and amazing, leaflets are reddish, and like that the climbers enwreathing at their tops are like their towering diadems and since those trees have golden fruits, they look as though decorated with golden jewellery. Those golden-bodied tress are shining forth like tender sun and their pedestals are completely studded with lapis gems. The birds encircling those trees are in the hue of lapis lazuli gems. The lotus lakes are encompassed with golden lotuses with broad petals, which in shine are similar to tender sun.
notes: Some mms use 'lofty trees' instead of the ' golden lotuses with broad petals' then it means that 'the stand of trees is surrounded by both the lotus-lakes and lofty trees...' In the next verse also some use the word 'tortoises' is used instead of 'lotuses.' This is said to be the problem with copyists.

glosses.meaning: golden, amazing, with bunches of lowers
with reddish, leaflets, as towering diadems
by their bodies, glittering, with golden, trees, also
blue, lapis lazuli gems, in hue, also
with lotus lakes [or, lotus-creepers,] dadR^ishuH = they beheld.

verses.devanagari:
जातरूपमयैः मत्स्यैः महद्भिः च अथ पन्कजैः
नलिनीः तत्र ददृशुः प्रसन्न सलिल आयुताः |
verses.iast:
jātarūpamayaiḥ matsyaiḥ mahadbhiḥ ca atha pankajaiḥ
nalinīḥ tatra dadṛśuḥ prasanna salila āyutāḥ |
verses.translation: Then they beheld there the lotus-lakes containing serene waters and stocky lotuses and burly fishes that are golden.

verses.devanagari:
कांचनानि विमानानि राजतानि तथा एव च
तपनीय गवाक्षाणि मुक्ता जाल आवृतानि च |
हैम राजत भौमानि वैदूर्य मणिमन्ति च
ददृशुः तत्र हरयो गृह मुख्यानि सर्वशः |
verses.iast:
kāṃcanāni vimānāni rājatāni tathā eva ca
tapanīya gavākṣāṇi muktā jāla āvṛtāni ca |
haima rājata bhaumāni vaidūrya maṇimanti ca
dadṛśuḥ tatra harayo gṛha mukhyāni sarvaśaḥ |
verses.translation: There the monkeys beheld choicest mansions everywhere made out of gold and silver, some with golden and some with silver domes, while some with golden and some with silver multi-stories, but all are studded with lapis gems with golden windows covered with laceworks of pearls. [4-50-30b-32a]

glosses.meaning: [ore purified by melting] golden, with windows

verses.devanagari:
पुष्पितान् फलिनो वृक्षान् प्रवाल मणि संनिभान्
कांचन भ्रमरान् चैव मधूनि च समन्ततः |
verses.iast:
puṣpitān phalino vṛkṣān pravāla maṇi saṃnibhān
kāṃcana bhramarān caiva madhūni ca samantataḥ |
verses.translation: They have also seen everywhere flowered and fruited trees that are similar in shine to red corals and rubies, and golden honeybees, as well as honeys.

glosses.meaning: red corals, rubies, similar in shine

verses.devanagari:
मणि कांचन चित्राणि शयनानि आसनानि च
विविधानि विशालानि ददृशुः ते समन्ततः |
हेम रजत कांस्यानाम् भाजनानाम् च राशयः
verses.iast:
maṇi kāṃcana citrāṇi śayanāni āsanāni ca
vividhāni viśālāni dadṛśuḥ te samantataḥ |
hema rajata kāṃsyānām bhājanānām ca rāśayaḥ
verses.translation: They beheld everywhere diverse and capacious beds and seats that are amazingly crafted with gemstones and gold, and also stacks of utensils made of gold, silver and bell metal.

verses.devanagari:
अगुरूणाम् च दिव्यानाम् चंदनानाम् च संचयम् |
शुचीनि अभ्यवहाराणि मूलानि च फलानि च
verses.iast:
agurūṇām ca divyānām caṃdanānām ca saṃcayam |
śucīni abhyavahārāṇi mūlāni ca phalāni ca
verses.translation: They saw the stockpiles of heavenly aloe vera substances and sandalwood sticks and depurated eatables, tubers and fruits.

verses.devanagari:
महा अर्हाणि च पानानि मधूनि रसवन्ति च |
दिव्यानाम् अम्बराणाम् च महा अर्हाणाम् च संचयान्
कंबलानाम् च चित्राणाम् अजिनानाम् च संचयान् |
verses.iast:
mahā ar.hhāṇi ca pānāni madhūni rasavanti ca |
divyānām ambarāṇām ca mahā arhāṇām ca saṃcayān
kambalānām ca citrāṇām ajinānām ca saṃcayān |
verses.translation: They have also seen top-grade soft drinks, luscious honeys, heaps of finest quality clothing, exotic blankets and sheaves of deerskins.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र तत्र विन्यस्तान् दीप्तान् वैश्वानर प्रभान्
ददृशुः वानराः शुभ्रान् जातरूपस्य संचयान् |
verses.iast:
tatra tatra vinyastān dīptān vaiśvānara prabhān
dadṛśuḥ vānarāḥ śubhrān jātarūpasya saṃcayān |
verses.translation: Vanara-s have also observed mounds of undefiled gold stockpiled here and there glowing with the glow of ritual fire.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र तत्र विचिन्वन्तो बिले तत्र महा प्रभाः
ददृशुः वानराः शूराः स्त्रियम् कांचित् अदूरतः |
verses.iast:
tatra tatra vicinvanto bile tatra mahā prabhāḥ
dadṛśuḥ vānarāḥ śūrāḥ striyam kāñcit adūrataḥ |
verses.translation: When searching here and there in that cavity those valiant vanara-s of high resplendence have perceived some lady rather not far from them.

glosses.meaning: of high, resplendence, valiant ones, Vanara-s

verses.devanagari:
ताम् च ते ददृशुः तत्र चीर कृष्ण अजिन अम्बराम्
तापसीम् नियत आहाराम् ज्वलंतीम् इव तेजसा |
verses.iast:
tām ca te dadṛśuḥ tatra cīra kṛṣṇa ajina ambarām
tāpasīm niyata āhārām jvalaṃtīm iva tejasā |
verses.translation: They saw a sainted lady there who is attired in jute-cloths and who is on a controlled diet and who is like a luminiferous entity by her own luminescence of asceticism.

glosses.meaning: jute- cloth, deer, skin, attired in
by her luminescence [of asceticism,] one who is glowing, as with
a sainted lady, at her, they saw.

verses.devanagari:
विस्मिता हरयः तत्र व्यवतिष्टन्त सर्वशः |
प्रपच्छ हनुमान् तत्र का असि त्वम् कस्य वा बिलम्
verses.iast:
vismitā harayaḥ tatra vyavatiṣṭanta sarvaśaḥ |
prapaccha hanumān tatra kā asi tvam kasya vā bilam
verses.translation: In wonderment the monkeys stood still all over, and in the matter of her identity Hanuma asked her, "Who are you? Whose cavity is this, either?

glosses.meaning: there [in that matter,] Hanuma, asked about

verses.devanagari:
ततो हनूमान् गिरि सन्निकाशः
कृत अंजलिः ताम् अभिवाद्य वृद्धाम् |
पप्रच्छ का त्वम् भवनम् बिलम् च
रत्नानि च इमानि वदस्व कस्य
verses.iast:
tato hanūmān giri sannikāśaḥ
kṛta aṃjaliḥ tām abhivādya vṛddhām |
papraccha kā tvam bhavanam bilam ca
ratnāni ca imāni vadasva kasya
verses.translation: Then Hanuma whose shine is similar to that of a mountain making palm-fold and reverencing that aged lady asked, "Who are you? Whose is this cavity, or the mansion or these jewels? Please speak."
